tip: -한테 usually means 'to', but with 빌렸어요 (billyeosseoyo = borrowed) it flips to 'from': 친구한테 (chinguhante) = from a friend. The verb decides the direction.
찾다 (chatda) normally means 'to find', but with money it means withdraw: 현금을 조금 찾았어요 (hyeongeumeul jogeum chajasseoyo) = I withdrew a little cash – you 'find' money at the bank.
잊어버렸어요 (ijeobeoryeosseoyo) contains 버리다 (beorida = throw away): tacked onto a verb it means done completely – and often regrettably. Forgot, gone.
Bills 'come out' in Korean: 카드값이 이번 달에 많이 나왔어요 (kadeugapsi ibeon dare mani nawasseoyo) = the card bill came out high this month. 나오다 (naoda = come out) is how charges show up.
Korean costs 'enter': 교육비가 정말 많이 들어요 (gyoyukbiga jeongmal mani deureoyo) = education really costs a lot, literally 'education money enters'. 들다 (deulda), no separate verb 'to cost'.
